name: Deliverable
description: Finished work put in front of the person who asked for it, with three ways to answer: approve it, say what to change, or turn it down.

deliverable_id.description: Stays the same every time this piece of work comes back, so round 3 is recognisably the same job as round 1.

asked_for.description: What was asked for, in the words it was asked in. Without it the reader is judging the work against their memory of the request.

summary.description: What was actually done, including anything deliberately left out.

url.description: Where the finished work can be opened. A description of the work is not the work.

alt.description: What the preview shows, for anyone who cannot see it.

content_hash.description: A fingerprint of the exact file or page being shown. An approval covers this version and only this version, so work that changes afterwards is not quietly covered by a decision made before it changed.

version.description: Which round of this work this is. The first time it is 1.

status.description: The status when this card was written. Anything decided after that is decided by the buttons below, and those decisions are recorded separately.

history.description: What happened to every earlier round of this work. Empty on the first round, and required to be honest after that.

what_happened.description: In one line: what was said about that round, or why it was replaced.

supersedes.description: The card this one replaces. It makes the chain of rounds followable rather than a set of separate messages that happen to share a title.

children.title: Earlier rounds of this work
children.text: What was said last time, and what it led to.

children.title: Close, but not right yet?
children.text: Say what to change instead of approving or rejecting. Whoever did the work gets your words exactly as you write them, and they stay on the record with the rest of this decision.

options.label: The words or the facts
options.description: Something written on it is wrong, missing, or out of date.

options.label: The look or the layout
options.description: It works, but it does not look right.

options.label: Part of it is missing
options.description: Something that was asked for is not there.

options.label: Wrong direction
options.description: Fixing details will not help. Start from somewhere else.

content_hash.description: Repeats the fingerprint shown on the card. When it is sent it must match the card, so an approval can never be read as covering a later version of the same work.

note.description: Anything to pass on with the approval.

selected.description: The areas ticked on the card. It may be empty; the written answer is what carries the request.

custom_input.description: What to change, in the reader's own words. Required, because a request for changes that does not say what to change is a rejection with extra steps.

reason.description: Why this is not wanted at all. Optional, because turning work down is allowed without a defence.

examples.name: First round of a rebuilt website

data.title: Tennant Group website
data.asked_for: Rebuild the site so it looks like the work we actually do, and make the phone number easy to find on a phone.
data.summary: The homepage, the about page and the contact form are rebuilt and live on a preview link. Everything from the old site is carried over except the news posts from 2019, which I left out because they read as out of date.
data.alt: The rebuilt Tennant Group homepage shown on a laptop and a phone

examples.name: Third round, after two sets of changes

data.title: Tennant Group website
data.asked_for: Rebuild the site so it looks like the work we actually do, and make the phone number easy to find on a phone.
data.summary: The phone number now sits at the top of every page on a phone, and the three testimonials you asked for are back on the homepage. Nothing else changed since round 2.
data.alt: The rebuilt Tennant Group homepage with the phone number pinned to the top on mobile

history.what_happened: You said the phone number was still hard to find on a phone.
You asked for the old testimonials back on the homepage.
